articles.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 review - the smartphone to open the floodgates for new foldable users - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- RATING
The new Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is a standout new product that establishes a whole new size, style and shape to take smartphones into the future. The Z Fold8 will be the onramp for many new mainstream customers to experience the delights of Samsung’s foldable form factor. And there will be no turning back.
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is literally changing the shape of smartphones and has provided a more accessible gateway for customers to graduate to a foldable device.
For eight years Samsung’s foldable devices have looked like regular smartphones and won a loyal band of customers who have stayed true to the form factor.
But it wasn’t for everyone – until now.
The new Galaxy Z Fold8 is smaller and shaped like a passport and is a lot more approachable for customers who had never considered a foldable smartphone before.
Many have found the previous models to be too big or too advanced to suit their needs.
Tech Guide has been using the Galaxy Z Fold8 for more than two weeks as our daily driver and have enjoyed the experience and the choices the device gives you on how you can consume your content.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 officially goes on sale this week and is priced from $2,699.
DESIGN
The first thing you notice is that new passport shape of the front 5.5-inch front screen.
It is shorter but wider than a regular smartphone display.
This comes in handy with the Z Fold8 because it makes it easier to do your everyday tasks like messaging an email right from that front screen.
And at this size it is comfortable to hold in your hand and easily fits in your pocket or bag.
It weighs just 201g when folded it is 123.9mm long and 81mm wide and 9.7mm thick.
When unfolded it is 123.9mm long, 161.4mm wide, and 4.5mm thick.
Even in the folded position the device is still fairly thin and not much thicker than a regular smartphone.
Galaxy Z Fold8 is easy to open and it smoothly unfolds to reveal the inside 7.6-inch display.
That’s all thanks to Samsung’s latest hinge design and its new Flex Titanium display that not only makes the screen more durable but enhances the quality as well.
And you can hardly see the crease when the screen is unfolded.
It has a fingerprint reader on the right edge below a volume rocker and a USB-C port on the bottom edge for fast charging.
On the rear panel is a small camera bump to fit the two 50MP cameras.
And the device has been built rugged with armour aluminium as well as Corning Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 to easily handle the daily grind.
It also has an IP48 rating, which is enough water resistance to protect it against accidental spills and splashes.
DISPLAYS
One of the complaints we had about the previous Fold devices was that the long narrow front screen didn’t provide us with enough room to comfortably type out our messages, which forced us to open the device to complete those easy tasks.
The bright and sharp front screen offers enough space to type while still offering enough room to see the message or email you’re replying to.
The front display of the Z Fold8 is about 5mm wider than the Galaxy S26 Ultra but is about 40mm shorter.
It doesn’t take long to get used to this new size and shape. We took to it pretty quickly.
We appreciated that wider front screen because we could do all those day-to-day tasks, viewing notifications and message replies without having to open the device.
It’s also still a comfortable size to scroll social media, look through our image gallery, and do everything else you would normally do with a regular size smartphone.
In some cases, especially when viewing social media, the front screen could barely fit one post on Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.
But the great thing about it was if we wanted to view things on a larger scale, all we had to do was open the device.
The inside 7.6-inch display has a 4:3 aspect ratio.
This means when you’re holding it in landscape it’s ideal for viewing video content.
Watching YouTube or streaming a show nearly fills the entire screen and delivers a result that’s even bigger than watching that same content on a regular smartphone held in landscape mode.
In fact, viewing a video on the Z Fold8 produces a larger image than you would see on the Fold8 Ultra. This is due to the Fold8 Ultra’s square inside screen that offers the same result no matter how you hold it.
That’s one advantage the Z Fold8 holds over the Fold8 Ultra.
It’s a 4:3 aspect ratio, which means that you can, like a regular smartphone, enjoy a landscape mode as well as portrait mode.
So if you want to read a book, scroll social media or browse a website on the Z Fold8, you simply turn it sideways to better display the content you’re enjoying.
It’s like having three screens in one.
And if you need to type with the device unfolded, the keyboard is a lot larger and adjusts whether you’re holding it in landscape or portrait mode.
There are still some apps that haven’t been fully adjusted for this new screen aspect ratio but we were still getting a bigger result than a regular smartphone.
MULTITASKING
The other advantage of having a larger display is the ability to run several apps at the same time.
We often had more than one app running on the larger inside screen so we could easily multitask.
There were times when we needed information from one app to use in an email or a message so being able have them side by side made it a whole lot easier.
Probably the best use of multitasking for us was recently at Optus Stadium in Perth when we were able to use our camera to shoot video on a pitch walk while viewing the the South Sydney Rabbitohs v Parramatta Eels match on Kayo Sports.
PERFORMANCE
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is powered by a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Mobile Platform for Galaxy chip.
Performance-wise the Z Fold8 did not skip a beat.
It was snappy and our apps opened instantly.
We were also able to switch between them in a split second and run them at the same time without any issues.
The chip offers enhanced CPU, GPU, NPU and AI performance has been designed to offer power-efficiency.
The new One UI 9 operating system was also smooth and easy to navigate.
CAMERA
On the camera side the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 two 50MP cameras on the rear panel to capture detail across wide and ultra-wide perspectives.
It also has a 10MP selfie camera on the 5.5-inch display and another 10MP selfie camera on the inside display.
There is also a mode to allow users to take selfies with the main cameras and use the front display to frame yourself.
The two 50MP cameras are quite capable and can capture some amazing images.
You don’t have the higher megapixel value of the Fold8 Ultra but that doesn’t stop users from capturing excellent pictures and shooting great video.
You can shoot 8K video at up to 30 frames per second on the Fold8, 4K at 30 or 60fps along with full HD and HD resolutions.
Another favourite feature was Dual Recording, where we were able to shoot video from the main cameras and the selfie camera at the same time.
This makes it possible to share your reaction to whatever you’re looking at whether it’s celebrating your team’s try or proudly watching your child while they are playing sport or performing.
You can choose to have the windows side by side, one on top of the other or inset.
We can tell you now the camera system of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is more than adequate to cover your photography needs.
BATTERY
The device has a 4,800mAh silicon carbon battery for enhanced performance and longer use.
And we can testify to the fact that it easily runs an entire day even when we’re using it as our daily driver and viewing the inside and outside screen constantly.
The Z Fold8 is a device that you will tend to use more to view content on that larger display.
We couldn’t keep our hands off it to watch various types of content wherever we were.
But despite this high use the battery performed admirably and got us through not only to the evening but also into the next day before we needed to think about charging.
THINGS WE DIDN’T LIKE
There’s lot to like about Galaxy Z Fold8 but having a phone of this size and shape does present some challenges.
Some apps don’t display properly on the smaller front screen with the bottom portion of some screens cut off and inaccessible. Most times opening the app on the larger inside screen helped us get around that.
Without a case, the Z Fold8 is not very grippy so be careful it doesn’t slip out of your hands.
Speaking of cases we think it would be a good idea to not only use a case to protect the device but to also look for a case with a stand to allow users to enjoy the larger screen hands-free.
The new Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is also expensive with prices starting from $2,699 for the 256GB variant.
But that new 256GB starting memory is double what was offered on previous foldable displays.
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 goes on sale this week.
VERDICT
The new Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is a standout new product that establishes a whole new size, style and shape to take smartphones into the future. The Z Fold8 will be the onramp for many new mainstream customers to experience the delights of Samsung’s foldable form factor. And there will be no turning back.

articles.title: Meshy 3D Agent: 3D-Modelle per Chat erstellen – ohne CAD-Software
articles.text:
KI-Agenten erobern die 3D-Welt – aber das eigentliche Problem ist ein anderes
Erst Code, dann Text, Bilder, Musik: KI-Agenten haben zuletzt eine kreative Disziplin nach der anderen übernommen. 3D galt lange als zu sperrig – zu viel Geometrie, Topologie und Textur für einen einzelnen Prompt. Mit dem Meshy 3D Agent soll auch diese Hürde fallen: Man beschreibt, was man will, und führt ein Gespräch, bis das Modell steht. Das klingt nach dem nächsten Hype – ist aber der falsche Reflex. Denn ein 3D-Objekt zu erzeugen, war selten das Problem. Die eigentliche Frage lautet: Lässt sich das Ergebnis auch benutzen?
Wie 3D bisher entstand
Klassisch entsteht ein 3D-Modell von Hand – in Spezialsoftware wie Blender, Maya oder ZBrush. Das ist ein Handwerk mit langer Lernkurve; wer es nicht beherrscht, vergibt jeden Auftrag nach außen. Die erste Generation von KI-Werkzeugen verkürzte das drastisch: Aus einem Prompt entsteht in Sekunden ein Modell. Doch das blieb meist ein Schuss ins Blaue – ein Prompt, ein Ergebnis, das man danach selbst nachbessert. Genau hier setzt der dialogbasierte Ansatz an.
Warum ein Dialog mehr ist als ein weiterer Generator
Der Meshy 3D Agent dreht dieses Prinzip um: Er schlägt Richtungen vor, erzeugt mehrere Varianten, verfeinert auf Zuruf und behält den Kontext. Statt zu raten, näherst du dich Schritt für Schritt einem nutzbaren Modell. Nach Angaben von Meshy ist es der erste vollständig dialogbasierte, mehrstufige Agent speziell für die 3D-Erstellung. Seit Kurzem steht er allen Nutzerinnen und Nutzern offen, zuvor lief er als Beta für zahlende Accounts.
Ein Praxisbeispiel: ein komplettes Set in einem Chat
Wie das praktisch aussieht, zeigt ein Beispiel aus der Spieleentwicklung. Ausgangspunkt ist ein einziges Referenzbild einer Szene – etwa eine Retro-Arcade-Kulisse mit Gebäuden, tropischen Pflanzen und Fahrzeugen. Im Chat löst der Entwickler die einzelnen Elemente heraus, erzeugt sie nacheinander in 3D und hält sie im selben Stil. Das Ergebnis ist kein zusammengewürfelter Haufen, sondern ein Set, das zusammengehört. Per Export wandern die fertigen Objekte nach Blender, wo die Szene entsteht. Genau das ist der Unterschied zu einem einzelnen Generator: nicht ein hübsches Modell, sondern ein stimmiges Set – in einem Durchgang, ohne zwölf Einzelteile mühsam aufeinander abzustimmen.
Was herauskommt – und in welchem Format
Nach Angaben von Meshy haben bis Juli 2026 mehr als 12 Millionen registrierte Nutzer über 100 Millionen 3D-Modelle auf der Plattform erstellt, die laut SimilarWeb gemessen am Web-Traffic die Nummer eins ihrer Kategorie ist. Das Unternehmen hat soeben eine Series-B-Finanzierungsrunde über 400 Millionen US-Dollar abgeschlossen – bei einer Bewertung von 1,5 Milliarden US-Dollar.
Als Eingabe reicht, was ohnehin da ist: ein Satz, ein Foto, eine Skizze. Ein texturiertes Modell entsteht laut Anbieter in rund einer Minute und lässt sich in acht Formaten exportieren (FBX, OBJ, GLB, USDZ, STL, BLEND, 3MF, DXF) – direkt in Engines wie Unity, Unreal oder Godot, in Blender und Maya. Für den 3D-Druck gibt der Agent wasserdichte STL- und 3MF-Dateien aus und prüft die Druckbarkeit vor dem Slicen; in Meshys eigenen Tests bestehen rund 97 Prozent der figurenartigen Modelle die Slicer-Prüfung in Bambu Studio. Die Übergabe an Slicer wie OrcaSlicer, Cura oder Creality Print erfolgt direkt.
Für Entwickler: Schnittstelle statt Oberfläche
Auch in eigene Workflows lässt sich der Agent einbinden: über eine REST-API, SDKs für Python und Node.js sowie offizielle Skill-Dateien für die Programmierassistenten Cursor und Claude Code. Ein KI-Assistent kann die 3D-Erzeugung damit direkt aufrufen – als Teil der Pipeline, nicht als isolierter Schritt.
Wofür sich das lohnt – und für wen
Der eigentliche Hebel ist nicht das einzelne Modell, sondern wer 3D überhaupt erstellen kann – und das betrifft nicht nur Spielestudios. Im Produktdesign verkürzt sich der Weg von der Skizze zum Prototyp, im Marketing entstehen 3D-Assets ohne eigene Pipeline. Wichtig bleibt: Der Agent nimmt die Fleißarbeit ab, Auswahl und kreatives Urteil bleiben beim Team.
Wo der Agent (noch) an Grenzen stößt
Ehrlich bleibt: Am stärksten ist die KI bei organischen Formen, Figuren und einzelnen Objekten. Bei präzisen geometrischen oder mechanischen Teilen mit engen Toleranzen wird es schwierig – generierte Kanten wirken oft weicher, als es eine Passung verträgt; hier bleibt klassische CAD-Software die bessere Wahl. Sehr feine Strukturen unter einem Millimeter, etwa dünne Antennen, können beim Druck brechen. Exakte Maße liefert er nicht von sich aus – sie müssen im Slicer nachgezogen werden. Und: Neue Modelle erzeugt er, vorhandene texturiert er neu – die Geometrie einer bestehenden 3D-Datei bearbeitet er nicht.
Lohnt sich der Test?
Wer das selbst beurteilen will, testet mit der Art von Objekt, die man wirklich braucht – nicht mit dem Vorzeige-Drachen, sondern dem eigenen Anwendungsfall. Weil die Generierung eine Zufallskomponente hat, lohnt es sich, mehrere Varianten zu erzeugen und die sauberste zu nehmen – und das Ergebnis vor Produktion oder Druck einmal durch Slicer oder Engine laufen zu lassen. Unterm Strich verschiebt der dialogbasierte Ansatz spürbar, was ohne Spezialsoftware möglich ist. Für Teams, die schnell von der Idee zum nutzbaren Modell kommen wollen, ist er einen Test wert. Ausprobieren lässt er sich bei Meshy.

articles.title: C'est historique : garder sa vieille voiture essence coûte désormais plus cher que passer à l'électrique
articles.text:
« Trop cher » : pendant des années, l’argument a suffi à refroidir les familles qui roulent à l’essence ou au diesel et qui lorgnaient sur l’électrique. La différence de prix à l’achat dépassait les économies de carburant, et le dossier s’arrêtait là. En 2026, ce raisonnement ne tient plus pour tout le monde.
C’est ce que met en avant I4CE (Institut de l’économie pour le climat), un cercle de réflexion qui publie chaque année son Observatoire des conditions d’accès à la transition écologique.
Pour jauger cette accessibilité, l’institut suit un ménage fictif, la famille Deschamps : deux parents, deux enfants, 3 900 euros de revenus par mois, une vieille maison rurale chauffée au fioul et une voiture thermique qui avale 16 000 km par an. Un profil de « classe moyenne inférieure« , très loin du cliché de la voiture électrique réservée aux cadres des grandes villes.
2025 contre 2026 : le basculement en un tableau
Reprenons les chiffres de l’Observatoire, mis en images par Alternatives Économiques dans son graphorama d’été. Ils comparent le budget mobilité mensuel de deux scénarios pour la famille Deschamps : garder sa vieille thermique, ou la revendre pour acheter une électrique d’occasion à crédit.
| Scénario | 2025 | 2026 | 
|---|---|---|
| Garder la vieille voiture thermique (budget mobilité complet) | 250 € / mois | 271 € / mois | 
| Électrique d’occasion, mensualités du crédit sur 6 ans | 203 € / mois | 157 € / mois | 
Deux mouvements se croisent. En gardant sa voiture, la famille voit sa facture passer de 250 à 271 euros par mois, portée par le carburant.
Dans le même temps, les mensualités du crédit sur six ans pour l’électrique d’occasion tombent de 203 à 157 euros, la revente du vieux modèle (2 500 euros) et l’achat d’une borne de recharge à domicile étant déjà déduits.
La ligne thermique correspond au budget mobilité complet, la ligne électrique aux seules mensualités. Mais une fois l’électricité, l’entretien et l’assurance ajoutés, des postes qui bougent peu, l’électrique reste malgré tout moins chère.
Pourquoi l’électrique d’occasion passe devant
Deux facteurs ont bougé en un an. D’abord le carburant. I4CE retient un litre d’essence passé de 1,77 à 2 euros entre 2025 et 2026, une hausse liée à la guerre au Moyen-Orient, qui gonfle mécaniquement le budget de ceux qui restent au thermique face à la crise à la pompe.
À l’inverse, le prix des voitures électriques a baissé et les taux d’intérêt aussi, l’Observatoire tablant sur un crédit à 1 %. Côté usage, un plein d’électrons revient de toute façon bien moins cher qu’un plein de gazole ou de sans-plomb.
Le marché de l’occasion suit le mouvement. Selon le baromètre de l’Avere-France et Mobilians, 50 868 électriques d’occasion ont changé de main au premier trimestre 2026, soit 27 % de plus qu’un an plus tôt, avec un prix moyen autour de 33 000 euros pour les modèles de moins de trois ans. De quoi confirmer que l’écart de prix avec le thermique se comble, et pas seulement sur le papier. D’autres analyses pointent la même bascule pour les gros rouleurs.
Attention tout de même : ce calcul vaut pour un ménage type, avec son kilométrage, sa possibilité de recharger à domicile et les aides du moment, et chacun devra refaire ses comptes. Mais la direction est tracée.
À l’horizon 2030, la thermique perdra l’essentiel de ses avantages, et l’électrique d’occasion devient un choix qui allège la facture autant qu’il soulage le climat.
Dernière précision : selon une étude allemande de 2024, remplacer sa voiture essence ou diesel par une voiture électrique neuve est toujours favorable pour le climat. Seul exception : les voitures parcourant moins de 3 000 km par an.

articles.title: Boeing is selling its air taxi startups to Archer Aviation
articles.text:
Boeing is selling three of its electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) subsidiaries to Archer Aviation, in addition to taking an undisclosed stake in the San Jose-based company.
Boeing is selling its air taxi startups to Archer Aviation
Archer will acquire the three subsidiaries, including Wisk Aero, for an undisclosed sum. Boeing will also take a stake in Archer.
The subsidiares to be acquired by Archer include Wisk Aero, which has been developing an autonomous electric aircraft; SkyGrid, which is building air traffic management systems to be used by urban air taxis; and Insitu, which makes high-altitude drones used by the US Navy. As part of the deal, Boeing and Archer will share technology and Boeing will retain access to Wisk’s autonomous flight systems for its current and next-gen commercial and defense projects.
The deal likely allows Boeing to re-focus on its finances on its core commercial airplanes, while also bolstering Archer’s position in the race to be the first to put electric air taxis into commercial service. Boeing is currently facing an enormous $715 billion backlog, representing over 6,200 planes that its customers have ordered that the aerospace giant has yet to build. The company is also under intense regulatory scrutiny following several notable safety incidents, including a Boeing 737 Max that lost a chunk of fuselage mid-flight in 2024.
Meanwhile, Archer has said it is planning to launch pilot air taxi services in several markets, including New York, Texas, and Florida, before the end of the year. The company is also positioning itself as a military supplier, having recently unveiled a new eVTOL aircraft co-developed with Palmer Luckey’s defense tech company Anduril.
“This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president, Commercial Airplanes Product Development, said in a statement. “It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses.”
Archer CEO Adam Goldstein called the deal “a watershed moment” that represents for Archer “the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform, rapidly growing our revenue base and bringing scale to our business.”
Wisk was formed in 2019 as a joint venture between Boeing and Kitty Hawk, the flying taxi startup bankrolled by Google cofounder Larry Page. Wisk has designed, built, and flown six generations of its eVTOL aircraft, amassing 1,700-plus flight tests. Notably, Wisk sued Archer in 2021 for allegedly stealing its trade secrets and infringing on its patents. The two sides settled the dispute in 2023, with Wisk agreeing to be the exclusive provider of autonomous flying technology to Archer.

articles.title: Intel "Nova Lake-S" iGPU with 12 Xe3P Cores to Feature 40 W PL2 and 20 MB of L2 Cache
articles.text:
Monday, August 10th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Intel "Nova Lake-S" iGPU with 12 Xe3P Cores to Feature 40 W PL2 and 20 MB of L2 Cache
According to the reliable Intel leaker Jaykihn, Intel's upcoming "Nova Lake-S," featuring 12 Xe3P cores, currently has a Power Limit 2 (PL2) setting of about 40 W. This builds on the previous rumor that this integrated graphics solution will arrive with two VCCGT phases for up to 65 W of power. This SKU includes four P-Cores, eight E-Cores, and four LPE-Cores, along with 12 Xe3P GPU cores. This 4+8+4 CPU core and 12 GPU core configuration is one of the few processors where integrated graphics require two VCCGT phases. In regular SKUs, VCCGT is a single-phase power rail for the integrated graphics inside the processor.
However, we now know that the PL2 setting will only use 40 W, as the 65 W threshold is set for extreme scenarios like PL3, and the graphics processor's PL4 is capped at that 65 W figure. The Xe3P features more microarchitectural changes compared to the Xe3 found in "Panther Lake." If readers recall, a 12 Xe3-core iGPU found in "Panther Lake" has 16 MB of L2 cache, while the Xe3P iGPU dedicated to "Nova Lake" will have a 20 MB L2 cache configuration, a 25% increase. More L2 cache means that some workloads will naturally benefit, but we still don't know preliminary performance. The Xe3P microarchitecture is expected to carry more changes, especially since it has a larger L2 cache.Depending on the SKU, Intel can include a single compute die for up to 28 cores total or two compute dies for a 52-core CPU SKU. It seems that the single compute die version will arrive first, with the dual compute die variants following. The 28-core "Nova Lake-S" DS version, a new SKU segment, is expected to launch in Q1 of 2027. For the regular overclocking-focused "K" SKUs, Intel reportedly plans an early Q2 launch between March and April. Since this is a single compute die SKU with 16 CPU cores and 12 GPU cores, we can expect to see it possibly within the first wave of the "Nova Lake" releases.

Don't hear me wrong, AMD has been lax on iGPUs for a while now. I'm still waiting on them to rise to the mobile iGPU challenge that Intel is throwing down. At this point, I think they just assume their CPUs will get paired with an NVIDIA dGPU in whatever form factor goes out, as AMD has largely given up on mobile dGPUs as well. The best they have there are RDNA3 chips that launched almost 3 years ago, to little fanfare.

articles.title: Autonomous welding startup TetraGen Robotics raises $1.8 million | BetaKit
articles.text:
Winnipeg-based autonomous welding robotics company TetraGen Robotics has raised $1.8 million CAD in seed round funding.
The news: The funding comes via an oversubscribed round led by Calgary’s StepChange Capital, with participation from Vancouver’s Emend Vision Fund, a VC firm with a focus that includes industrial modernization. TetraGen did not disclose cheque sizes or additional investors, but did say that it received funding from Jim Richardson of Winnipeg’s James Richardson & Sons.
From the source: Founded in 2022 by former University of Manitoba Intelligent Digital Manufacturing Lab founder Matt Khoshdarregi, TetraGen’s tech combines the traditional chassis of a welding robot with proprietary AI software and machine vision. The company markets its robots as being “manual programming-free,” meaning they do not require humans to set up complex welding instructions and can automatically generate programming to adapt to real-world circumstances.
The context: The Canadian collaborative robot market is valued at just over $52 million, but is projected to expand to more than $129 million in the coming years. Focusing on breaking into industries like heavy equipment, mining, and defence manufacturing, where manual programming and weld complexity remain high, TetraGen told BetaKit it will use the $1.8 million to accelerate commercialization, aiming to deploy more autonomous systems to customers throughout North America. TetraGen did not say where its systems are currently deployed, and where they will target expansion first, but said that success will be measured by “increasing customer deployments, expanding our commercial footprint, [and] strengthening strategic partnerships.”
TetraGen said it also plans to use the capital to grow its engineering and commercial teams, but did not say how many hires that might result in.
Final thought: Autonomous robots, sometimes called “cobots,” are increasingly common in industrial welding, with the Canadian Welding Bureau updating its official standards in 2025 to reflect the change. Likewise, many post-secondary institutions now include robotics in their curriculum. As Canada looks towards a shortage of skilled trades workers in welding, robotic systems are seen as a way to bridge the gap.

articles.title: Samsung lança TVs Mini LED no Brasil com foco em IA, games e casa conectada
articles.text:
A Samsung anunciou nesta segunda-feira (10) uma nova linha de TVs Mini LED no Brasil. Os aparelhos chegam como uma alternativa mais acessível para consumidores interessados na tecnologia, com modelos de 50 a 100 polegadas e recursos de inteligência artificial, entretenimento e conectividade.
A novidade foi apresentada pela Samsung Brasil e combina tecnologias de imagem, recursos para esportes e games, serviços gratuitos, integração com dispositivos inteligentes e ferramentas de áudio. A empresa posiciona a linha como uma porta de entrada para recursos que antes estavam concentrados em televisores de categoria premium.
Entre os principais diferenciais estão o Vision AI Companion, o Samsung Gaming Hub, o SmartThings, o Modo Futebol e o sistema operacional One UI Tizen, que terá suporte a atualizações por até sete anos.
Nova linha aposta em Mini LED e inteligência artificial
Os novos televisores estão disponíveis nos tamanhos de 50, 55, 65, 75 e 85 polegadas, além de uma versão de 100 polegadas. Segundo a fabricante, a proposta é ampliar o acesso à tecnologia Mini LED sem abandonar recursos avançados de imagem, inteligência artificial e conectividade.
A tecnologia utiliza LEDs significativamente menores que os empregados em painéis convencionais. Com isso, o sistema consegue controlar de maneira mais precisa as áreas de iluminação da tela, favorecendo níveis mais elevados de contraste e reduzindo efeitos indesejados em cenas escuras.
O processamento de imagem também recebeu recursos baseados em inteligência artificial. O sistema pode aprimorar conteúdos de resolução inferior para até 4K e ajustar parâmetros da imagem de acordo com o material exibido. A identificação automática de cenas também permite modificar a reprodução das cores conforme o tipo de conteúdo.
Outro recurso de destaque é o Vision AI Companion. A ferramenta permite interagir com a televisão por comandos de voz e utiliza inteligência artificial generativa e conversacional. A solução combina Bixby e Gemini para responder perguntas relacionadas ao que aparece na tela ou sobre outros assuntos durante a utilização do aparelho.
A experiência não fica restrita à imagem. O sistema sonoro pode adaptar suas características de acordo com filmes, músicas e jogos, além de oferecer efeito surround virtual em 3D. Há ainda ajustes relacionados ao horário e à cena apresentada. Para quem utiliza determinadas Soundbars da marca, a função Sincronia Sonora permite combinar os alto-falantes do televisor com os da barra de som.
Futebol, karaokê e jogos também fazem parte da proposta
Para transmissões esportivas, a linha conta com um modo específico para futebol. A ferramenta altera a reprodução de áudio e imagem para reforçar a percepção da torcida e tornar as cenas mais vibrantes, de acordo com a fabricante.
No entretenimento cotidiano, a Samsung reúne diferentes serviços na chamada proposta de TV Tudo em 1. O Samsung TV Plus oferece centenas de canais gratuitos, com conteúdos que incluem filmes, notícias, esportes, novelas, programas infantis e música. O acesso não depende de assinatura, embora exija conexão com a internet e uma conta Samsung.
Outra opção é o karaokê integrado ao aplicativo Stingray Music. Nesse caso, o celular pode ser utilizado como microfone, com acesso a um catálogo de mais de 100 mil músicas. A compatibilidade depende do aparelho utilizado e requer os aplicativos indicados pela fabricante.
Para os jogadores, o Samsung Gaming Hub reúne serviços de jogos em nuvem, incluindo Xbox Cloud Gaming e NVIDIA GeForce NOW. A proposta permite acessar títulos sem fazer downloads e sem utilizar um console dedicado, embora determinados conteúdos possam exigir assinatura, conexão à internet ou controle separado.
Nos modelos compatíveis, a televisão também alcança taxa de atualização de até 120 Hz em resolução 2K. O suporte ao VRR contribui para uma exibição mais fluida, reduzindo interrupções e oscilações durante as partidas.
SmartThings transforma a TV em central da casa
A integração com o ecossistema SmartThings amplia a função do televisor para além do consumo de conteúdo. A plataforma permite controlar e monitorar mais de 1.000 dispositivos compatíveis com os padrões Zigbee e Matter.
Entre as possibilidades estão a criação de rotinas automatizadas, o acompanhamento do consumo de energia e o funcionamento de determinadas funções mesmo quando a TV está desligada. O recurso Home Insights utiliza inteligência artificial para sugerir automações com base nos hábitos do usuário.
O smartphone também pode assumir o papel de controle remoto inteligente. Pelo aplicativo SmartThings, é possível movimentar o cursor na tela e navegar por aplicativos e conteúdos.
A fabricante também incorporou mecanismos voltados à segurança. A Central de Segurança Knox protege os dispositivos conectados e busca reduzir riscos de acesso não autorizado e exposição de dados. A plataforma inclui ainda uma Central de Senhas e opções de login por QR Code.
Atualizações prometem prolongar a vida útil
Um dos compromissos anunciados para a nova linha é a oferta de atualizações do sistema operacional por até sete anos. A estratégia pretende manter os aparelhos compatíveis com novos recursos e evoluções da plataforma ao longo do tempo.
Além das atualizações, o software pode adaptar recomendações de conteúdo aos hábitos de cada usuário. A Samsung afirma que a experiência continuará evoluindo com novos recursos e funcionalidades desenvolvidos para a plataforma.
Os televisores também contam com mecanismos de gerenciamento energético. Sensores identificam a iluminação do ambiente e ajudam a ajustar o brilho da tela, enquanto o sistema analisa as cenas para administrar esse parâmetro e contribuir para a redução do consumo.
No acabamento, a linha adota o chamado Design MetalStream, baseado em uma estrutura metálica. A proposta combina o aspecto visual do material com robustez e integração a diferentes estilos de ambiente.
Preço e disponibilidade
A nova linha de TVs Mini LED da Samsung chega ao mercado brasileiro com preços a partir de R$ 3.039,05. A oferta contempla modelos de diferentes dimensões, incluindo a versão de 100 polegadas.
A empresa também informa que determinados recursos podem variar conforme o modelo, o tamanho da tela, o país, os aplicativos disponíveis e os serviços de terceiros. Algumas funções dependem de conexão à internet, conta Samsung ou acessórios vendidos separadamente.
Wagner Edwards é Bacharel em Jornalismo e atua como Analista de SEO e de Conteúdo no Olhar Digital. Possui experiência, também, na redação, edição e produção de textos para notícias e reportagens.

articles.title: Decathlon réduit de 400 euros le prix de son VTT électrique Stilus OffRoad+ doté de 110 km d'autonomie
articles.text:
Decathlon propose de nombreux vélos électriques pour différents usages, notamment plusieurs modèles de VTT électriques conçus pour la randonnée tout-terrain. Ces vélos sont particulièrement adaptés aux sorties à la campagne, aux chemins forestiers et aux parcours vallonnés, tout en restant suffisamment polyvalents pour être utilisés sur route ou pour les trajets du quotidien. Le Stilus OffRoad+, un puissant VTT électrique semi-rigide, actuellement en promotion, en est l’exemple parfait.
Le vélo électrique Decathlon Stilus OffRoad+ est lancé à 2 199,99 € en mars 2026. Il est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion au prix de 1 799,99 € chez Decathlon. Seules les tailles M/L sont encore disponibles. La promotion est valable jusqu’au 28 août 2026.
C’est quoi, ce VTT pour les randonnées ?
Le Decathlon Stilus OffRoad+ reprend le look sportif d’un VTT, avec un cadre fermé en aluminium qui privilégie la rigidité et la stabilité. Cette conception le rend un peu moins facile à enjamber qu’un vélo à cadre ouvert, mais elle se montre particulièrement adaptée à une pratique plus sportive et aux longues randonnées. Sa fourche Suntour XCM 34 offre 120 mm de débattement pour absorber une bonne partie des chocs et des irrégularités, tandis que ses larges pneus CST Patrol de 29 pouces participent au confort et à la stabilité.
Côté performances, le Stilus OffRoad+ mise sur un moteur central Star Union CM5001 capable de délivrer jusqu’à 500 W et surtout un couple pouvant atteindre 110 Nm au démarrage, avant de se stabiliser à 76 Nm. De quoi faciliter les démarrages en côte, les montées et les passages avec un peu de dénivelé. La transmission repose sur un dérailleur Shimano CUES à 9 vitesses, associé à une cassette 11-46 dents, une configuration pensée pour offrir suffisamment de polyvalence lors des randonnées. Les freins à disque hydrauliques Shimano MT200 viennent compléter l’ensemble.
À ce prix, le Stilus OffRoad+ est-il une bonne affaire ?
Moins de 1 800 € pour un VTT électrique de Decathlon, c’est encore une belle somme, mais c’est aussi une très bonne affaire pour un deux-roues performant. Le Stilus OffRoad+ propose cinq modes d’assistance, permettant d’adapter le comportement du moteur aux différents moments de la randonnée, avec notamment un mode piéton pratique pour accompagner le vélo à pied dans les passages difficiles.
La principale amélioration par rapport au Stilus OffRoad lancé en 2025 concerne l’autonomie. Le Stilus OffRoad+ embarque une batterie intégrée de 720 Wh, contre 504 Wh sur son prédécesseur. Decathlon annonce ainsi jusqu’à 110 km d’autonomie, contre 70 km auparavant. Un écran LCD couleur de 2 pouces permet de suivre les principales informations de conduite, tandis que les éclairages, catadioptres, sonnette et fixation pour porte-bidon complètent l’équipement.

articles.title: When Credentials Are No Longer Enough: Device Trust in the AI Era
articles.text:
Identity security is under growing strain. The passwords, multi-factor authentication (MFA) responses, IP reputation, geolocation and browser characteristics organizations have traditionally used to judge whether a login is legitimate are becoming easier for attackers to steal, imitate or work around.
AI is adding to that pressure, not by creating a completely new class of attack, but by making familiar identity attacks faster and more efficient. Meanwhile, rotating IP addresses and disposable browser profiles make malicious logins harder to distinguish from legitimate ones.
Against this rapidly evolving threat landscape, organizations need effective Zero Trust measures that protect against ‘legitimate’ logins from attacker-controlled infrastructure. It’s here that device trust helps, ensuring that valid credentials are insufficient without the device context they were meant to be used from.
The Industrialization of Account Takeover Attacks
AI has not created a fundamentally new form of account takeover. Attackers still rely on familiar techniques: phishing, credential theft, MFA abuse, session hijacking and social engineering. What has changed is the amount of manual work needed to run those attacks effectively.
Threat actors can create and send thousands of convincing phishing emails with little effort. If a more personalized message is needed, AI can pull public information from across the internet to build a detailed profile of the target.
Attackers can then adapt their message to match the target’s language and business context. A finance employee might receive a supplier-related request, while an administrator is approached with a cloud access issue.
None of this means AI is autonomously running the entire intrusion. In most cases, people still choose the targets, control the infrastructure and decide what to do with successful access.
The more accurate way to describe the change is that AI compresses the human work between acquiring information and acting on it. It lowers the cost of personalization and triage, allowing teams to run more campaigns and focus their effort on accounts with the highest expected value.

Where Traditional Trust Signals Are Falling Short
Identity platforms often combine several signals to decide whether a login should be trusted. Each still has value, but attackers increasingly know how to steal, imitate or bypass the evidence these controls rely on.
Credentials
While passwordless options are becoming more popular, credentials are still required in most authentication flows. As such, phishing and credential-harvesting malware like infostealers form the first step in many account takeover attacks.
Attackers can also simply reuse credentials from previous breaches. In an incident earlier this year, IGN’s Twitch stream was hijacked by an unknown attacker, using Restream.io credentials that had sat in infostealers dumps for roughly a month before being exploited.
The attack highlights the importance of scanning for leaked credentials. Solutions such as Specops Password Auditor carry out a read-only scan of your Active Directory to identify leaked passwords and related vulnerabilities.
You’ll then receive an easy-to-understand report to help you prioritize fixes. Download Specops Password Auditor for free here.
MFA
MFA significantly improves security, but its strength depends on the method and the surrounding authentication flow.
One-time codes can be captured through phishing. Push notifications can be abused through repeated prompts or social engineering. Adversary-in-the-middle phishing can relay credentials and MFA responses to the legitimate service in real time.
Attackers may also steal session cookies after authentication and avoid the MFA challenge entirely.
IP Address and Geolocation
IP reputation can identify connections from known malicious infrastructure, while geolocation can flag activity from an unexpected region.
However, attackers can route traffic through residential proxies, mobile networks or compromised systems. They may choose an exit node close to the victim, making the login appear geographically plausible.
Legitimate activity is equally difficult to interpret. Remote work and corporate VPNs can produce unfamiliar locations. Stricter policies may block more attacks, but they also increase false positives and support work.
NIST’s Zero Trust Architecture guidance reflects this limitation. SP 800-207 states that organizations should not grant implicit trust based solely on physical or network location.
It treats user and device authentication as separate functions that should take place before access to an enterprise resource is established.
Device Binding Adds Another Trust Layer
Most identity controls still depend on credentials that can be presented from almost anywhere. This is why organizations need to extend trust decisions beyond traditional identity signals.
Solutions like Specops Device Trust limit an attacker’s ability to spoof legitimate login attempts and reduce the risk of account takeover by:
1. Tying Access to Approved Hardware
Organizations should be able to register and limit trusted devices, different policies to corporate, personal and third-party hardware.
If the login comes from an unknown device, the identity platform should treat that as a meaningful change in risk. Access shouldn’t be granted simply because the credentials and MFA succeeded.
2. Continuously Evaluating the User and the Device
A successful login should not create permanent trust for the rest of the session. Access should continue to depend on both the user’s identity and the health of their device.
If posture changes, such as through disabling endpoint protection or the device falling out of compliance, the level of access should change.
3. Matching Enforcement to the Level of Risk
Security teams are right to be cautious about adding friction, so device posture policies do not have to make every issue a blocking event.
Depending on the application and the severity of the problem, organizations can reduce privileges or give the user a short grace period to fix the device.
That approach keeps the control proportionate. A missing update should not always be treated in the same way as disabled endpoint protection or a rooted device.
4. Making it Easy for Users to Restore Trust
When access depends on device health, users need a clear way to resolve problems. Self-guided remediation allows employees to fix issues quickly, which reduces disruption while keeping the required security standard in place.
Mitigate the Risk of AI-Enabled Account Takeover with Specops
As AI improves the speed and personalization of account takeover, IT teams need solutions that blunt the effectiveness of those attacks.
While it may be a challenge to identify every malicious login from network signals alone, organizations can make valid credentials insufficient without the device context they were meant to be used from.

articles.title: Corporate Data Stolen in Levi Strauss Cyberattack
articles.text:
Denim company Levi Strauss & Co on Friday disclosed a cyberattack that affected certain corporate data stored on employee computers.
The incident, it said in a Form 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), was the result of social engineering and affected three employees’ company-issued computers.
The company says its immediate response and containment actions have resulted in the attackers’ eviction from the compromised computers.
“Based on preliminary findings from the company’s investigation, the company believes that certain corporate information was accessed and exfiltrated as a result of the incident,” Levi Strauss told the SEC.
According to the company, the investigation into the attack is ongoing, but based on the preliminary findings no customer data appears to have been stolen.
“The company has not experienced any interruption in business operations as a result of the incident,” Levi Strauss said.
The company also said it did not believe that the incident “has had, or is reasonably likely to have, a material impact”.
Levi Strauss did not say who was behind the attack or whether it received any extortion demands, and has not shared details on the type of social engineering the threat actor used.
According to some unconfirmed reports, however, UNC6671, a hacking group behind multiple recent voice phishing (vishing) campaigns, might have been involved.
SecurityWeek has emailed Levi Strauss for additional details on the data breach and will update this article if the company responds.

articles.title: Sorpresa en el Apple Watch Series 12: Apple revivirá un modelo icónico que los fans adoraban
articles.text:
Por si las vacaciones de verano te han descolocado, te recordamos que la keynote de Apple para conocer los nuevos iPhone, Apple Watch y otras sorpresas está, más o menos, a un mes de distancia. Y eso significa que los rumores y las filtraciones son rutina durante estas últimas semanas. Hoy toca hablar sobre las palabras de Mark Gurman en su recién publicado boletín semanal: según él, Apple está preparando una sorpresa mayúscula para los Apple Watch Series 12.
De hecho, menos mal que ha surgido alguna filtración sobre estos relojes, porque durante los últimos meses apenas han tenido protagonismo en las publicaciones de los expertos, lo que avanzaba que podríamos estar ante una generación bastante continuista. Esto no ha cambiado demasiado, pero la última afirmación de Gurman nos deja con una novedad más que interesante.
No para todo el mundo, pero sí para quien quiera renovar su reloj con un Apple Watch Series 12, quiera un dispositivo sumamente resistente a los arañazos y, además, tenga un presupuesto más bien amplio. Apple tendría todo listo para volver a introducir en su catálogo un material que en el pasado demostró ser muy interesante.
Los Apple Watch Series 12 podrían tener una versión de cerámica, aunque no será para todo el mundo
Si hace poco que te has interesado por Apple y sus productos, ya te lo adelantamos: los relojes de cerámica no son nuevos en su catálogo. La compañía lanzó una versión del Watch Series 2 con este material, volvió a utilizarlo en el Watch Series 3, la descontinuó en la cuarta generación y la utilizó por última vez en los Watch Series 5 de 2019.
Desde entonces, la cerámica no ha vuelto a tener cabida en los relojes de la compañía, pero hoy Mark Gurman ha afirmado que Apple está trabajando en una versión con este material para los Apple Watch Series 12 o 13. Es decir, para este año o el que viene.
¿Qué ventajas tiene la cerámica? Sería uno de los materiales más especiales de los nuevos Apple Watch Series 12, pues la naturaleza de la cerámica hace que el reloj sea mucho más resistente a los arañazos y permite tener un dispositivo brillante con un tacto y un aspecto impresionante durante años.
El último Apple Watch de cerámica se lanzó en color blanco y está considerado como uno de los favoritos de los fans, aunque este material no es para todo el mundo. Su principal problema es el precio. A pesar de que la cerámica no suena como algo carísimo o exclusivo, el último reloj en incluirlo (Series 5) costaba 1.299 dólares en 2019, lo que se podría traducir en un monto aún más caro a día de hoy.
Gurman no tiene del todo claro que vayamos a ver un Apple Watch Series 12 de cerámica en septiembre, aunque una afirmación así por su parte se puede tratar como información sumamente importante, lo que significa que en algún momento todo apunta a que la compañía volverá a introducir la cerámica en la ecuación.

Fichiers administratifs à classer, mails à rédiger, devoirs des enfants à envoyer… Chaque rentrée apporte son lot d’obligations et on est vite submergé. La solution ? Tout centraliser.

articles.title: Record ou arnaque ? Il parcourt près de 2 000 km en électrique sans jamais brancher sa voiture
articles.text:
La voiture électrique n’a définitivement pas fini de faire parler d’elle, surtout qu’elle est arrivée en tête des ventes le mois dernier dans notre pays. Pourtant, les freins psychologiques demeurent. C’est le cas de l’autonomie, bien plus limitée que sur les modèles thermiques. Nissan tord le cou à cette idée reçue en tenant un nouveau record à sa botte : 1 980 km parcourus d’une traite, ça parle !
Une performance spectaculaire… mais en trompe-l’œil
Alors, à qui doit-on cette performance spectaculaire ? Impossible que ce soit la Micra, vu que sa batterie est limitée à 52 kWh. La nouvelle Leaf, alors ? Avec ses 75 kWh et 622 km annoncés en WLTP, c’est déjà plus probable. Hélas pour elle, ce n’est pas non plus notre championne. Car Nissan n’a pas utilisé une électrique comme les autres pour réaliser cet exploit. Il s’agit en réalité d’un modèle équipé d’un prolongateur d’autonomie.
La surprise sous le capot : ce n’est pas le modèle que vous croyez
La palme revient ainsi au Qashqai avec sa technologie e-Power. Le SUV a parcouru les 1 980 km séparant Bogota de la côte des Caraïbes. Le trajet, qui s’est déroulé du 14 au 17 juillet, n’a nécessité aucun arrêt pour ravitailler. Si elle n’est pas inédite, la solution retenue par Nissan demeure aussi efficace qu’originale. Le véhicule dispose bien d’un électromoteur et d’une petite batterie de 1,97 kWh.
Le secret de cette autonomie XXL enfin dévoilé
Mais là s’arrêtent les similitudes avec une voiture électrique traditionnelle. Le japonais a en effet recours à un trois-cylindres de 1.5 l développant 158 ch et 250 Nm de couple. Ce dernier n’est pas relié aux roues, mais à un générateur produisant de l’électricité alimentant la minuscule batterie. Il se distingue particulièrement par son excellente efficience permise par son taux de compression variable, une rareté sur un véhicule de série.
Une consommation d’essence qui fait de l’ombre au diesel
De quoi déjouer les difficultés du parcours, allant des zones urbaines bouchonnées à des sections plus roulantes. Si les 1 980 km sont bluffants pour un modèle électrique, ils ne sont pas moins impressionnants avec un hybride. Vu que le réservoir peut contenir jusqu’à 55 litres d’essence, cela correspond à une consommation de carburant de 2,8 l/100 km. Mieux qu’un diesel, donc !
Un record mondial homologué et des technologies qui font des envieux
Le record a été validé par le Guinness Book en octroyant au Qashqai e-Power le titre du « plus long trajet effectué par un véhicule électrique à autonomie prolongée non rechargeable ». Dans la gamme européenne de Nissan, c’est le Qashqai qui est équipé de la technologie e-Power aux côtés de son grand frère, le X-Trail. Les Japonais, eux, sont plus chanceux en disposant de la Note e-Power qui aurait un certain potentiel chez nous.

articles.title: Son agent Claude devait simplement lui réserver un cours de sport, l’IA a fini par pirater la salle
articles.text:
ABC News présente l’affaire comme le premier cas australien connu de cyberattaque autonome menée par un agent d’intelligence artificielle.
Le 9 août 2026, le média public consacre un article à l’histoire d’Andrew, un habitant de Melbourne employé par une entreprise vendant des produits d’IA. Le twist de son témoignage ? Avoir vu son agent IA pirater sa salle de sport après lui avoir simplement demandé de gérer ses réservations à sa place.
Du simple créneau à la faille exploitée
L’objectif initial d’Andrew était relativement simple : confier à son agent, utilisé via OpenClaw et connecté à Claude, la réservation manuelle des séances sur l’application de sa salle de sport.
La tâche est effectuée en quelques minutes. L’agent précise au passage avoir trouvé un moyen de réserver des créneaux plusieurs semaines à l’avance, alors que le système ne devait normalement pas le permettre. Une faille dans le logiciel de réservation, découverte sans qu’on le lui ait demandé.
Andrew, alors quatrième sur liste d’attente pour un cours plus tard dans la semaine, demande à son agent s’il est possible de le faire remonter dans le classement. L’agent franchit alors une ligne supplémentaire. Plutôt que de se contenter d’explorer les options légitimes, il teste directement l’annulation de la réservation du premier de la liste.
Selon les messages envoyés à Andrew, l’API de réservation ne comportait « aucun contrôle d’autorisation » sur l’annulation des réservations appartenant à d’autres utilisateurs. Le test fonctionne, et la manipulation fait passer Andrew de la position 4 à la position 3.
Réalisant la portée de ce qui vient de se produire, Andrew demande aussitôt à son agent d’annuler l’opération et de restaurer la réservation de l’usager évincé. Sans succès, l’agent lui répond ne pas être en mesure de rétablir la place de l’autre client.
Les agents IA, prêts à tout pour réussir leur mission
Selon le média australien, l’agent aurait ensuite présenté ses excuses à Andrew pour cette action non sollicitée, puis rédigé, à sa demande, un e-mail destiné à alerter l’éditeur du logiciel de réservation sur la vulnérabilité qu’il venait d’exploiter.
Pour l’heure, ni l’éditeur du logiciel de réservation, dont l’identité n’a pas été rendue publique, ni Anthropic n’ont commenté l’incident. À ce stade, aucune analyse technique indépendante ne semble avoir eu accès au système concerné pour confirmer la nature exacte de la faille.
Reste que sur X, l’affaire ravive les discussions autour de la capacité des agents IA à poursuivre leurs objectifs coûte que coûte. Elle survient quelques jours après une série d’incidents observés lors de tests internes, où plusieurs agents IA seraient sortis de leur environnement de test, allant jusqu’à pirater d’autres entreprises pour parvenir à leurs fins.

articles.title: Member of The Com sent to prison for blackmail, sextortion
articles.text:
A member of "The Com," a loose-knit online cybercrime collective that targets children and teenagers, has been sentenced to two years in prison for blackmail and sextortion offenses against nearly 120 victims worldwide.
20-year-old Justin Swaddle from Leeds (known as 'Epstein', 'Rugen' and 'Moscow' on Snapchat, Telegram, and Discord) was first arrested in October 2023 by West Yorkshire Police.
Swaddle was sentenced today after pleading guilty to multiple child sexual abuse offenses and blackmail at Leeds Crown Court on July 2. He will also be added to the National Sex Offenders Register and will be subject to a Sexual Harm Prevention Order for 10 years.
"Justin Swaddle targeted young and vulnerable victims all over the world to abuse and scare them into carrying out shocking self-harm and sexual activity, purely to gain popularity with his peers online," said NCA operations manager Danielle Pownall.
"He gained the trust of his victims, before collecting private information about them so he could threaten to share their intimate images or report them to their school or parents to incite further content.
After taking over the investigation in January 2024, the UK National Crime Agency (NCA) identified 117 female victims worldwide, aged from 13 to 17.
While searching seized devices, the investigators also found images of children with ages ranging from three to 17, several of them showing the result of acts encouraged by Swaddle.
"Telegram messages recovered from Swaddle's device showed he had attempted to incite a child to sexually abuse a younger child and record it for him, threatening to leak indecent images if further content was not received," the NCA said.
"Numerous images were found on his device showing victims with self-harm injuries, including Swaddle's aliases being carved into their skin, and indecent images of children in Categories A to C, with A being the most severe."
The Com (short for Community) recruits and grooms victims through online platforms, coercing them into self-harm, violence, and the production of child sexual abuse material, often through blackmail.
As Europol reported earlier this year, the Com collective is organized into multiple subgroups, including:
- Offline Com: promotes property damage, harming others, and committing acts of terrorism,
- (S)extortion Com: coerces minors into sex crimes and encourages self-harm and suicide,
- Cyber Com: orchestrates network intrusions and ransomware attacks,
- 764: a subgroup that surfaced in 2021, notorious for grooming young people into producing explicit content later used for extortion or shared among members.
Two alleged 764 leaders (21-year-old Leonidas Varagiannis and 20-year-old Prasan Nepal) were arrested in April 2025and now face life in prison for operating an international child exploitation ring.
The Com was previously linked to ransomware attacks against Las Vegas casino breaches in September 2023 and, more recently, UK retailing giants Marks & Spencer, Co-op, and Harrods in April 2025.
In February, a year-long Europol-led operation dubbed "Project Compass" led to 30 arrests and 179 suspects being linked to The Com. Europol has also flagged 4,340 URLs for removal during a multi-week July operation targeting online content tied to the Com group.

articles.title: OpenAI met en pause son modèle Astra : il pourrait être trop doué pour les cyberattaques
articles.text:
Écrire un mail, générer une image, vous mettre en scène dans une vidéo créée de toutes pièces… Voilà le genre de chose que l’on associe à l’usage de l’intelligence artificielle générative. Mais il ne faut pas oublier que derrière ces fonctionnalités se cache une puissance potentiellement dangereuse, si elle n’est pas contrôlée.
C’est pourquoi OpenAI, derrière le célèbre ChatGPT, s’est dotée en 2023 d’un guide définissant jusqu’où ses modèles de langages peuvent aller dans différents domaines : cybersécurité, biologie, chimie et capacité à s’améliorer eux-mêmes. Si un modèle atteint un seuil trop élevé sur l’échelle fixée, l’entreprise revoit sa copie.
Pour prendre un exemple : il serait inconcevable qu’OpenAI sorte un modèle capable de mener des cyberattaques d’un nouveau genre, pour lesquelles nous n’avons aucune défense. Voilà pourtant ce dont serait capable Astra.
Astra, nouveau modèle d’OpenAI, est trop puissant
Selon ses propres critères, OpenAI ne peut exclure qu’Astra ait atteint le seuil « critique » en matière de cybersécurité. C’est-à-dire qu’il est « capable d’identifier et de développer, sans intervention humaine, des exploits « zero-day » fonctionnels de tous niveaux de gravité dans de nombreux systèmes critiques réels et hautement sécurisés », ou « concevoir et mettre en œuvre de bout en bout des stratégies novatrices de cyberattaques contre des cibles hautement sécurisées, en ne disposant que d’un objectif général. »
À titre de comparaison, GPT-5.6 Sol, modèle le plus puissant d’OpenAI à ce jour, est au seuil « élevé ». Ce qui suffit pour autoriser son déploiement. Astra, lui, devra patienter. La suite de son développement se fera sous un cadre plus contraignant, accompagné de mesures de sécurité plus strictes. Par exemple, des environnements de tests isolés ou un accès restreint au réseau.
OpenAI indique aussi collaborer « avec les organismes publics concernés et certaines organisations spécialisées dans la sécurité de l’IA afin de tester les capacités de ce modèle ». Et ce, « afin de garantir que les capacités de pointe de modèles tels qu’Astra, et de ceux qui suivront, soient mises en œuvre de manière responsable et à grande échelle, dans l’intérêt de l’humanité tout entière ».
Un sens des responsabilités louable que les plus cyniques auront tôt fait d’associer à un coup marketing. Un peu comme a pu le laisser penser Anthropic avec son annonce de Claude Mythos, l’IA trop dangereuse pour le grand public.

articles.title: Panduit E36G18L PDU Review A Sweet Managed and Switched by Outlet PDU
articles.text:
Recently, we had the opportunity to take a new Panduit PDU for a spin. The Panduit E36G18L PDU includes per-outlet monitoring and switching, management, and more. We even got to take the temperature monitor for a spin. We have a ton of photos for a PDU review, so we are going to organize this to take you through the device a little differently from how we would show you a server, a network switch, or even a low-cost PDU.
Panduit E36G18L Plugs and Outlets Overview
One of the biggest challenges with reviewing a Zero U PDU is simply how to photograph it. The unit is 2″ x 3″ but then it is 70″ long. Here is what the full unit looks like on the STH studio’s 2nd set.
Starting off, the PDU that Panduit sent has a NEMA L6-30P plug, which is for a 30A 208V circuit. This is a plug we have been using in some of our data center lab racks for over a decade at this point.
A 3m/10-foot cable connects the plug to the PDU, and we get a Panduit logo.
Pandiut’s design has two banks with magnetic breakers. Here is one of the breakers.
Here is the second. You can see these banks are labeled as teal and grey just to make it clear which downstream outlet is on each breaker.
If we wanted to find the corresponding outlets, here we can see that outlets 31-36 correspond to the B2 bank.
There are a total of 36 outlets, but you may think they look different. That is because there are 18 “4-in-1” combination outlets that can accept C13, C15, C19, or C21 power plugs interchangeably. There are also 18 “2-in-1” combination outlets accepting both C13 and C15 plugs.
Another feature is that each outlet has an individual status LED. Here they are lit up:
Another feature is that you can use locking cables in these. Here we have a Panduit LPCA08 installed.
This cable, aside from being blue to match STH colors, is dual-locking compatible with standard C14/C13 connections as well as W-Lock and V-Lock PDU outlets.
Here is a close-up of the C14 side.
Here is the C13 side of the cable.
While the plugs and outlets are undoubtedly important, this is not just a simple power strip. Instead, we have management features built-in.
Let us get to the smarts of the PDU next.

articles.title: Critical Flaws Discovered in Belgian eID Software Used by 2 Million People
articles.text:
DEF CON — A security researcher has revealed severe, now-resolved security vulnerabilities in the Connective digital identity system, a browser extension used by over two million users in Belgium.
Developed by Nitro Software Belgium, the software is used by eight of Belgium’s ten largest banks and over 60 government agencies to manage digital identity authentication and execute legally binding electronic signatures.
James Arnott, security researcher and founder of cybersecurity firm Bay Area Labs, discovered that the software failed to verify which website was attempting to communicate with the user’s computer. Because these checks were missing, any website or embedded online ad could interact directly with the Connective application running on a victim’s machine without their knowledge or permission.
According to Arnott, a malicious website could silently read connected electronic ID (eID) and payment card details. Furthermore, attackers could trick users into revealing their eID PIN by triggering official-looking authentication pop-ups. Because the software allowed web pages to customize the text inside these dialog boxes without displaying the domain making the request, users had no way to verify whether a prompt was legitimate or a phishing attempt.
When a user entered their PIN into a prompt, the application transmitted it back to the requesting webpage. An attacker could then use the PIN to generate unauthorized approval tokens to forge legally binding electronic signatures whenever the victim’s physical eID card was inserted into a card reader.
The compromise of the eID system severely impacted the trust model of Belgium’s broader digital ecosystem, including government portals like CSAM.be and third-party identity providers like Itsme.
While these service providers contained no flaws of their own, their reliance on eID signatures meant that an attacker with stolen signing capabilities could register or hijack digital identity accounts.
In addition to identity theft, the researcher uncovered a remote code execution vulnerability that operated independently of whether an eID card was plugged in. By exploiting a flaw in how the application processed files on the local computer, a malicious website could force the software to execute attacker-controlled code at the user level.
An attacker could execute this drive-by attack by tricking a user into downloading a file disguised as a standard document and visiting a webpage. Requiring no special permissions, the flaw also carried the risk of spreading like a self-propagating worm by hijacking user credentials to send malicious links to other potential victims.
Nitro fully remediated the issues 146 days after the initial report and awarded a $200 bug bounty. The company deployed updates to block unauthorized origin requests and secure PIN handling, with final security enforcement completed in late July. No CVEs appear to have been assigned.
Nitro has not responded to SecurityWeek’s request for comment.
Arnott publicly disclosed the findings at DEF CON and released a blog post with additional technical details.

articles.title: Steam hardware shipper breach leaks customer data, including names and addresses
articles.text:
Valve says a data breach may have exposed the personal information of customers who ordered its Steam hardware in Europe. In an email sent to users, Valve says its European shipping partner, CEVA Logistics, suffered a data breach that may have included customer names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses.
Steam hardware shipper breach leaks customer data, including names and addresses
The incident impacts customers who ordered Steam devices in Europe.
The breach at CEVA occurred between July 29th and August 1st, weeks after Valve began taking reservations for its new Steam Machine and Steam Controller. Valve adds that European customer data “was likely compromised” as part of the breach, as CEVA stores “delivery-related information” for up to 90 days after orders.
As a result of the breach, Valve says to “expect fake messages” over email, text, or on the phone that claim to come from Steam, Valve, or a delivery company. “They may quote your address back to you to prove they’re genuine. They may ask you to confirm a delivery, pay a small customs or redelivery fee, or sign in somewhere to ‘verify’ your order,” Valve says. “Treat all of them as fake.”
The notice says additional data linked to users’ Steam accounts or purchases wasn’t impacted, adding that CEVA “does not have access to your payment information, passwords, Steam Guard codes or other information.” Valve notes that it only deals with account issues from help.steampowered.com, and won’t contact users over email, Steam chat, or Discord.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo do Windows usa 5 vezes mais RAM que no Mac • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Previsão do tempo do Windows usa 5 vezes mais RAM que no Mac
Aplicativo Clima do Windows 11 pode consumir mais de 1 GB de RAM. Por ser basedado no Webview2 (motor de navegador), a sua otimização não é tão fácil.
O Windows 11 tem alguns recursos que consomem mais memória do que o razoável. Um deles é o aplicativo Clima, que fornece informações meteorológicas variadas, mas pode ocupar 1 GB ou mais de RAM, sendo até cinco vezes superior nesse parâmetro do que a ferramenta de clima nativa do macOS.
Pelo menos é o que afirma o Windows Latest. Testes feitos pelo veículo mostraram o aplicativo Clima consumindo mais de 1,2 GB de RAM, mesmo quando a ferramenta ficava em segundo plano.
Coincidentemente, eu falei do app Clima no texto sobre a Microsoft reconhecer que alguns dos aplicativos do Windows 11 exageram no consumo de memória.
Na ocasião, eu usei o Clima como exemplo, destacando que a ferramenta consome entre 600 MB e 900 MB de RAM. Já era um padrão de consumo alto, mas o Windows Latest constatou que o app pode ir ainda mais longe nesse parâmetro.
Que fique claro que o Clima (também disponível no Windows 10, só para constar) é um aplicativo muito interessante. Ele fornece informações detalhadas sobre temperatura, precipitação (chuva), qualidade do ar, vento e assim por diante. Também é possível usá-lo para acompanhar a previsão do tempo de várias cidades ao mesmo tempo.
Muitas dessas informações são exibidas em gráficos e até em mapas. A dúvida que fica no ar é: os aspectos positivos da ferramenta justificam tamanho consumo de RAM? Bom, podemos presumir que o nível de detalhamento do aplicativo Clima demanda muitos recursos gráficos.
Mas também temos que levar em conta que este, na verdade, é um “web app”, ou seja, um aplicativo que depende de um “motor” de navegador — no caso, o Edge WebView2, baseado no Chromium. Nessas circunstâncias, é muito mais difícil otimizar o consumo de RAM.
Há mais um pequeno complicador: o Clima exibe anúncios, afinal, corresponde ao MSN Clima (um serviço totalmente web) sob uma embalagem ligeiramente diferente.
Infelizmente, ainda não há nenhuma informação sobre isso. Mas, como o Windows Latest destaca, se a Apple consegue fazer o seu aplicativo de previsão do tempo consumir por volta de 250 MB — sem exibir anúncios —, a Microsoft também.
Podemos manter alguma esperança com relação ao aplicativo Clima. Recentemente, a Microsoft prometeu otimizar o desempenho do Windows 11 em PCs com 8 GB de RAM. Na mesma publicação, a companhia ressaltou que vem trabalhando na “otimização da eficiência dos componentes Chromium e Webview2”. Quem sabe isso não beneficie o app Clima em algum momento?

articles.title: Transformer Lab wants to automate research with new AI tool Primus
articles.text:
Kitchener-Waterloo-based AI research startup Transformer Lab has launched what co-founder and CEO Ali Asaria said is “the most ambitious thing I’ve ever been a part of.”
For the past two years, Transformer Lab’s four-person team has been quietly working to fully automate the research process.
“We see this as the next revolution, the one that actually replaces what we currently call the AI revolution.”
Ali Asaria,
Transformer Lab
Today, Transformer Lab announced it has opened access to the fruit of that labour, Primus, an autonomous research tool Asaria claims can connect users with AI agents capable of producing “PhD-level” research in a small fraction of the time as their human counterparts.
A global shortage of machine learning (ML) engineers has constrained AI progress; Asaria hopes Primus can fix that, and more.
“If you work in a neolab, but you can’t hire the best [ML] engineers because there’s only so many of them in the world, and most of the best ones are going to these few companies, well, now you have access to as many of them as you want at the touch of a button,” Asaria told BetaKit in an interview.
Asaria teamed up with co-founder Tony Salomone, who worked at Asaria’s previous retail tech startups Tulip and Well.ca, to build Transformer Lab in 2024. The AI research lab officially launched earlier this year with funding from a group that includes Toronto’s Ripple Ventures and Kitchener-Waterloo’s Garage Capital.
Since forming, Transformer Lab has been spending time with researchers to understand their processes step-by-step and automate them.
Primus projects run dozens or hundreds of different agents, which each use different AI models appropriate to their respective tasks, Asaria said. Some are tiny, while others are frontier models from big-name providers. The company is also training models of its own.
Transformer Lab claims Primus can turn a single prompt-based research question from a hypothesis to a completed research paper in “hours to days” without additional human direction.
Using Primus, Transformer Lab claims that it has produced and published 30 “Masters to PhD-level” research papers in 30 consecutive days across domains ranging from materials science to physics, the interoperability of large language models, seismology, protein design, audio generation, and 3D vision. While Transformer Lab did not provide more detail on how these papers were assessed to be at that level, one of them has already received a citation in published research by the Google DeepMind team.
With Primus, Asaria hopes to play a part in ensuring more than just a few tech giants own the AI future, and accelerate the pace of research across all sorts of scientific domains—beyond just ML. “We see this as the next revolution, the one that actually replaces what we currently call the AI revolution,” he said.
RELATED: Ali Asaria’s Transformer Lab launches worldwide
Transformer Lab has made Primus free to start, and is rolling it out to the public on a waitlisted basis, admitting researchers and developers as AI compute capacity permits.
“We’re a small team, and we have plenty of ideas that get shelved because we lack the resources to execute them,” Rubric Labs co-founder and CEO Sarim Malik said in a news release. “With Primus, it feels like adding a team of world-class, senior ML engineers to your roster overnight who can chip away at your ideas.”
Asaria is also conscious that tools like Primus could ruffle some feathers. Some academics have expressed doubt that AI can oversee the entire research pipeline; as Alessandra Buccella wrote for The Conversation, “the very existence of science as a source of authoritative knowledge about the natural world fundamentally depends on human life.”
Transformer Lab is trying to be thoughtful about how it deploys the product, including by specifying in its terms that users are not allowed to submit the papers it produces to journals and ask human volunteers to review them.
Asaria thinks a shift to more AI-powered research ultimately stands to benefit humanity, but “needs to be done carefully.”
Feature image courtesy Mauricio J Calero for BetaKit.

articles.title: Europe expands its Starlink rival to 348 satellites as IRIS² moves into implementation — €15.6 billion network will boost EU government capacity by 60%, with launches starting in 2029
articles.text:
Europe expands its Starlink rival to 348 satellites as IRIS² moves into implementation — €15.6 billion network will boost EU government capacity by 60%, with launches starting in 2029
66 new satellites are earmarked for defense, security, and emergency services,
The European Commission and the SpaceRISE consortium signed an implementation agreement on Friday, August 7, to roll out Europe’s IRIS² satellite constellation, moving the project from the planning and negotiation stage into full-scale deployment. According to an official press release, the agreement adds 66 satellites to the planned constellation, bringing the total to 348 — 330 satellites in low Earth orbit and 18 in medium Earth orbit — with first launches targeted for 2029.
The expansion is intended to substantially increase the network’s government and defense capacity. According to the Commission, the revised architecture will provide 60% more secure governmental communications capacity within the EU and 54% more globally. The existing satellites in the baseline constellation will also receive additional functionality and stronger security features, while the 66 new spacecraft will operate in higher low Earth orbit.
IRIS² — short for Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity, and Security by Satellite — is the European Union's flagship secure-connectivity constellation, intended to give European governments an autonomous alternative to foreign networks such as SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon's Leo. The Commission signed a 12-year concession contract for the program in December 2024 with the SpaceRISE consortium — a grouping of European satellite operators SES, Eutelsat, and Hispasat — which is building and operating the system under a public-private partnership alongside manufacturers including Airbus Defense and Space, Thales Alenia Space, OHB, and Aerospacelab.
Once operational, the multi-orbit network will deliver sovereign, encrypted connectivity to authorized governmental users across EU member states and participating non-EU countries, currently Norway and Iceland, for use in emergency response, critical infrastructure protection, and security missions, with capacity also earmarked for citizens in areas with poor coverage.
When the concession contract was signed in December 2024, IRIS² carried a price tag of €10.55 billion ($12.19 billion), funded by the European Union, the European Space Agency, and the SpaceRISE consortium. The accelerated timeline and larger constellation have pushed that figure higher, with the consortium's partners now putting total planned investment above €15.6 billion ($18.03 billion), drawn from the EU budget for 2028–2034, ESA, the consortium partners, and member states. Several countries have already committed, with Poland and Hungary pledging €656 million ($758 million) and €500 million ($578 million), respectively, while Spain has announced between €1.6 and €2 billion ($1.85–2.31 billion).
IRIS² is frequently framed as Europe's answer to Starlink, as they are both satellite constellations aimed at providing connectivity to dead zones. However, the primary purpose of the 348-satellite-strong constellation is more niche. The EU wants an independently controlled communications system — mainly for government and emergency use, but also for civilian applications — that can remain available when terrestrial networks fail, or when access to foreign-operated satellite systems becomes politically or strategically uncertain. On the other hand, Starlink’s growing 10,000-satellite constellation is a mainly commercial, privately owned company selling broadband to consumers worldwide. It is now also running satellite-to-phone internet services through Starlink Mobile.
